<!-- pr-reviewer: 3d0a5d397a5081a0e86e3b4713aedc701d26ab51 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Deciding M5 review of head 3d0a5d3; read in full and built locally, merged with current upstream/main.)

**What looks good**
- Not stacked on anything: base is `main`, the merge-base is on upstream/main, the diff against main is the 10 files listed, and the trial merge is clean. The #1738/#1717 mention is only an overlap note: #1738 is a draft based on `issue/1648-wcs-page-work-offset` and #1717 is a separate PR (`needs-rework`). Neither is a parent, so this merges on its own. #468 and #1209 (both `conflicts`) touch other functions and will refresh at their own merge time.
- Existing machines are byte-identical. The only shipped machine with a C rotary is `millturn.mch` (`axis [0,0,1]`). For +Z or an unstated axis, `c_z_sense` is +1, `liveCSense` is 1, `outC = 1 * C`, and the travel is unflipped. No golden files, `.nc` files or snapshots are touched. `golden_cl`, `recorded_streams`, `recorded_post_streams` and all the `script_*` suites pass unchanged.
- -Z is mirrored in one frame everywhere. Stamped C stays canonical (right-hand about +Z) for the simulation and CL. `stamp_c_about` flips the travel to `[-hi,-lo]` for the gate and unwind. `c_letter_problem` judges `sign*c`, the posted word, against the stated travel. `fanuc-lathe.cps` posts `liveCSense*C`, and `lastC`, the C delta, the composite feed scaling and the posted-word cap all use the same negated value. The post reads only the travel flag, so the gate is the single travel check and it agrees with the post. `-0` is normalised by `trim0`.
- Arcs: `stamp_c` emits only `arc: None` chords, so no G2/G3 direction can flip under the reversed sense. The original arc's sagitta is checked before the chord cap, and non-finite endpoints or centres are refused by name. The pinning test also checks full-helix chaining and the -450 deg end.
- The Rust and .cps refusals match: finite-but-huge vectors are scaled before squaring, the same 0.998 Z-alignment test is used, and non-Z, zero and non-finite C vectors are refused by name in the gate, the machine check and the post (`liveStart`). No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests.
- Process: no process files, dependencies, build.rs or `.github` changes. It has a decision file (`docs/decisions/33-c-sense-and-arcs.md`), a `Changelog:` line and `Refs #33`. Files are under 400 lines.

**Results (locally, merged with main, debug)**
- camcraft-cl + camcraft-post, all targets: 642 passed, 0 failed. This includes `script_fanuc_lathe` (18, with the 3 new -Z and non-Z tests), the direction unit tests and `cl::rotary` (arc pin and chord-limit refusal).
- camcraft-sim `c_axis_fixture`: 9 passed.
- camcraft-app: lib 341 passed (1 ignored). Suites run: `c_axis_live_world` (3), `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `c_axis_fixture`, `setup_sheet`, `machine`, `axis_direction`, `rotary_letter`, `rotary_verify`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `rotary_field_parity`, `rotary_fixtures`, `rotary_subplate`, `lathe_workholding_live`, `lathe_workholding_mill_post`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `lathe_post`, `inverted_axis_display`, `golden_cl`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `machine_edit`, `posting`, `mcp_live`, `mcp_rotary_stack`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `doosan_dnm_a_state`, `kept_parts_live`, `setup_mounts_post`, `recorded_post_streams`. All 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run by me: the slow motion/app lanes and the ui suites. The ui suites are not touched, and the author's batch gate covers the rest. No GitHub workflow was dispatched.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- A C rotary whose stated axis is non-Z (or zero) was previously accepted silently by the gate. It is now refused by name when a spindle-C move is stamped or checked. No shipped machine is affected, and this is the intended behaviour.
- The Fanuc-control feed for the C composite and real-machine -Z behaviour are still unverified on hardware, as the PR body already says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
